hero.title: Document with Confidence,
hero.desc: Thiqa is the trusted hub for multi-signature document verification. Collect digital signatures, preserve validity proof for each, and give any party instant confidence in your documents.

card.ocsp: OCSP proof saved for each signature at the moment of signing

features.title: Why Thiqa?
features.heading: Trust is not a promise.
features.f1Text: Full cryptographic verification of every signature using certified government PKI certificates.
features.f2Text: Manage contracts requiring multiple signatories with full order and clarity.
features.f3Text: OCSP evidence captured at signing time proves the certificate was valid when used.

howItWorks.title: From Document
howItWorks.desc: Thiqa is designed to make the signing and verification lifecycle clear for all parties, from creator to signer to verifier.
howItWorks.s1Text: Upload the document or register its digital fingerprint and specify the required parties.
howItWorks.s2Text: Each party signs their digital fingerprint without sharing the document content.
howItWorks.s3Text: Share the verification code and let any party confirm document validity in seconds.

security.title: Every Signature Carries
security.desc: We don't just verify the signature. We verify the certificate chain, capture the OCSP status at signing time, and store it as immutable proof.

cta.title: Ready to Authenticate What Matters?
cta.desc: Start building your organization's digital trust layer today.

guide.intro: This guide covers the complete issuer lifecycle: generating cryptographic keys, obtaining a certificate from EJBCA, registering on Thiqa Hub, initiating a document, signing it, and revoking or verifying it as needed.
guide.whatYouWillAchieve: What you will achieve in this guide:
guide.achieve1: Generate EC Key Pair and Certificate Signing Request (CSR)
guide.achieve2: Obtain Certificate from EJBCA via REST API
guide.achieve3: Register as an Issuer in Thiqa Hub
guide.achieve4: Initiate Document and Calculate its Hash
guide.achieve5: Sign the Document using CAdES-BES and submit
guide.prereq1Details: Required for CAdES-BES signing (-cades flag). Check with openssl version
guide.prereq2Details: To parse JSON safely. Install via package manager
guide.prereq4Details: Client certificate and private key for mTLS on EJBCA REST API
guide.prereq5Details: Certificate Profile, End Entity Profile, and CA Names
guide.prereq6Details: Connectivity to EJBCA (port 8443) and Thiqa Hub (port 8081)
guide.step1Desc: Generate an Elliptic Curve (EC) key pair on the P-256 curve and a Certificate Signing Request (CSR).
guide.step1Callout: Replace YOUR_ISSUER_NAME with the Issuer Name (e.g. Ministry of Health), YOUR_ORGANIZATION with your Org name, and YOUR_COUNTRY with a two-letter country code (e.g. SD).
guide.issuerKeyDesc: Your private key. Keep it safe and never share it.
guide.issuerCsrDesc: The signing request sent to EJBCA.
guide.step2Desc: Send the CSR to the EJBCA REST API to obtain a signed certificate and its CA chain.
guide.step2bDesc: EJBCA returns a PKCS7 container. Extract individual X.509 certificates as PEM:
guide.step2Tip: Alternative: If enrolled via EJBCA web interface and downloaded a P12 file, extract key and cert with:
guide.step3Desc: Send the extracted certificate chain to Thiqa Hub. The Hub validates the chain against the root CA, checks OCSP status, and registers you as an Issuer.
guide.step3Callout: The certPem field MUST contain the full certificate chain (Leaf + Intermediates). Sending only the leaf will cause a chain validation error.
guide.step4Desc: Generate a unique Document ID, print a QR code containing it on the document, then calculate the Hash and register it in the Hub.
guide.step4aTitle: 4.1 — Generate Document ID and Print QR Code
guide.step4aCallout: Print a QR code containing the document ID () on the PDF BEFORE proceeding. The QR must be included now because the Hash is calculated on the final document content.
guide.step5Desc: Sign the Document Hash using CAdES-BES and submit it to the Hub.
guide.step5aCallout: The -binary flag is mandatory. Without it, OpenSSL silently truncates input at null bytes, producing an invalid signature that the Hub will reject.
guide.step5bCallout: status will be VALID if the required quorum is met, or PENDING_SIGNATURES if more signatures are needed.
guide.step6Desc: To revoke a document, call the revoke endpoint. Revocation is permanent — a corrected document must be initiated as a new record.
guide.step7Desc: After signing, you can verify document validity at any time. The Hub re-verifies all signatures and returns the current status.

flowDiagram.n1Details: Extract private key (issuer.key) and certificate chain (issuer.pem) from EJBCA via OpenSSL.
flowDiagram.n2Details: Send certificate chain to Thiqa Hub for root verification and register account for signing.
flowDiagram.n3Details: Generate UUID, compute PDF SHA-256 hash, and send to platform to initiate. Print QR on document prior to this.
flowDiagram.n4Details: Sign hash locally via OpenSSL in CAdES-BES format, and submit encrypted signature.
flowDiagram.n5Details: Permanently revoke document if there is an error. Future verifications will fail.
flowDiagram.n6Details: Verify document validity, all issuer signatures, and their OCSP status at signing time.
